newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African govt warns of tough trade talks with EU.
newsitem.headline: S.African govt warns of tough trade talks with EU.

text.p: The South African government on Tuesday expressed its disappointment at the harsh terms laid down by the European Union (EU) for a free trade deal between the two regions.
Addressing the South African Chamber of Business's 1996 Convention, Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin warned that a round of tough trade negotiations was approaching.
"If we had any hopes that there would be some remarkable political initiative to support South Africa's development drive, then those hopes have been dashed," Erwin said.
"We are basically in hardnosed trade negotiations with the EU...You'll be tough, we'll be tough," he said.
The EU's negotiating mandate, put on the table in March, has been slammed by South African parliamentarians for being too protectionist as it excludes the country's major agricultural products.
Earlier this month the Agriculture Ministry threatened to pull out of negotiations if there was no improvement in the terms offered by the EU.
South Africa's mandate is expected to be ready by the end of the month.
Erwin said the EU in drafting tough terms had missed an historic opportunity to contribute to overall economic growth in Africa.
"I think it is a pity...As I have said to the EU it is not us losing an opportunity but it is you that are losing an opportunity to make a substantial contribution to the development of Africa.
"It holds a great deal of prospects for the future for everyone."
Erwin said South Africa would not offer the EU any greater access to its markets than that enjoyed by its neighbours in the Southern African Development Community (SADC).
"In my view it is quite obvious that we should not offer the EU more preferential access than we offer our neighbours in SADC."
South Africa's 11 partners in SADC have expressed concern about a trade agreement with Europe, fearing hefty losses in customs revenue. A meeting of member states is underway in Namibia this week.
